summary: Brentwood sits at the eastern edge of Contra Costa County where the Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta meets the flanks of Mount Diablo, and that geography defines nearly everything about daily life — summers regularly push into the 90s and beyond, a stark contrast to the fog-cooled Bay Area cities just 50 miles west, yet the nearly 9.6 hours of daily sunshine and cool delta breezes at night (lows averaging 51°F) keep evenings comfortable. The surrounding landscape is still visibly agricultural — orchards, vineyards, and u-pick farms border newer subdivisions — giving the city open-sky horizons that feel more Central Valley than Bay Area suburb. That agricultural fringe, however, masks a clear bedroom-community reality: with no major employer base in town, most working households commute west toward Walnut Creek, Oakland, or San Francisco, often via Highway 4, a corridor notorious for congestion that a recent BART extension to nearby Antioch has only partially relieved. A median home price around $792,000 against a median household income near $140,000 puts the price-to-income ratio at roughly 5.7 — stretched but less punishing than inner Bay Area cities, which is precisely what draws buyers eastward. Brentwood is essentially a bet that delta-edge space and sunshine are worth the commute that comes with them.
